correctness.rationale: The exact Schur complement of the assembled nodal Gram matrix yields signed evaluation kernels; edgewise absolute integration yields the exact norm. A 21-term positive coefficient certificate proves strict leaf dominance for all integers d>=2 and real t>0, and two explicitly factored polynomial identities plus Descartes sign changes prove the crossing at d=9 and unique finite maximum only for d>=9. Limits are direct asymptotic expansions. A standalone symbolic checker verifies the critical polynomial identities and independently assembled exact rational matrices for 35 parameter pairs; finite checks corroborate but do not substitute for the proof.

originality.rationale: This is a first two-hub, tunable-bridge metric-tree projector with a sharp d=9 resonance and unique interior maximum. The previously recorded sharp star formula has one hub and gives only the separate-star limit 7/3 envelope; it neither dominates the two-hub graph nor implies the demonstrated overshoot. Kayumov treats interval L-splines, Oswald planar simplicial triangulations, while Boman concerns general weighted finite-element estimates. Actual indexed mathematical findings queries did not retrieve a dominating or equivalent exact two-hub statement. Residual uncertainty about unindexed work and Boman full text is acknowledged.
residual_risks: Unindexed paper, thesis, or other terminology may contain an equivalent exact symmetric double-star formula.
Full text of Boman 2006 was unavailable; no whole-paper noncoverage inference is made.

value.rationale: Two-hub metric trees are the minimal topological departure from one-hub stars, a natural setting for testing the stability of least-squares spline projections under network structure. The first finite two-hub family beating the sharp 7/3 star-family envelope occurs exactly at d=9, with a unique bridge length maximizing the amplification. Complete optimizer location, sharp all-parameter constants and first-order singular bridge scaling give a motivated structural classification and a useful counterboundary to one-hub intuitions.
